ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis marks latitude, and near the equator corresponds to 0°; the horizontal arrow above is labeled "value increases", indicating that the farther right the curve is, the larger the value is. There are three curves in the figure, among which the salinity curve protrudes to the right near the low-latitude subtropics, but is relatively leftward near 0° at the equator. Then reason: the question asks about the characteristic of the salinity of surface seawater near the equator, so it is only necessary to compare the position of the salinity curve near 0° with the high-value area on the right. Since the salinity curve near 0° is not in the high-value area on the right, but is leftward, this shows that the salinity value is not high; therefore, the salinity of surface seawater near the equator is relatively low.
